Why teams adopt it

The control layer for local agent work.

Omni Code does not replace your editor or terminal. It makes the existing desktop session easier to supervise across devices, with approvals, voice, and reply shaping built into the loop.

Operating model

Mobility without giving up local control.

Core idea

Your machine keeps the real coding context.

The bridge stays close to the desktop workflow, while the client becomes the remote surface for sessions, messages, approvals, and notifications.

Transport

HTTP for commands. SSE for live updates.

The setup is simple enough to self-host and explicit enough to reason about in team environments.

Security posture

Tokens and client IDs are configurable.

Bridge URL, token, and allowed client IDs can be matched to the environment you actually run.

Workflow

One loop from terminal to remote control.

The product is strongest when the coding agent already runs on a desktop machine and needs a reliable remote surface for supervision.

01 / Session flow

Attach the client to your bridge

Point Omni Code at the desktop bridge running on your machine or LAN.

Use the current bridge URL or override it in settings, then pair with the token and client ID expected by the bridge.

Current scope

What Omni Code optimizes for.

Area What Omni Code emphasizes
Session access Continue or inspect desktop agent sessions from mobile or desktop clients.
Human review Approval prompts can stop sensitive actions and wait for an explicit answer.
AI approval Low-risk requests can use AI-assisted approval before falling back to a person.
Voice loop Speech input, auto-play replies, and text-to-speech reduce terminal babysitting.
Infrastructure Bridge-based, configurable, and friendly to self-hosted setups instead of a fixed SaaS backend.
Reply shaping Brief-reply mode can ask the AI to compress what it did into a much shorter summary.
Distribution Android updates can come from GitHub releases or a self-hosted bridge manifest.
